_about: Curated judgements for the status report (owner: status-reporter). Read by scripts/status_report.py together with docs/features.json and the live board, gates and ledger. Everything here is a judgement that must be traceable to evidence ids listed under 'evidence'; the script refuses to render if the judgements contradict the gate checklists. Written for a technically capable reader who does not know the repo: spell out abbreviations, no file names or task ids in the executive fields.

project.name: HX Stomp Tone Matcher
project.goal: Give the tool a song and get back a preset for the Line 6 HX Stomp guitar pedal that sounds like the guitar on the recording, checked on the real pedal. It works by trying candidate presets, comparing the sound with the recording, and adjusting until they match.

health.rationale: Nothing is blocked, but the main bet is in doubt. The first blind listening on real songs (five songs, the five best drive candidates against the separated guitar) drew 'so bad I can't even compare them'. That contradicts the open listens of 22 October that called the same kind of match 'pretty good', and a blind listen is the stronger evidence. Nothing computed from a recording sets the reverb: a pre-registered pilot found no agreeing signal, and the estimator built afterwards held on one song of two. The pass bars for the sealed drive test are proposed, not approved, so the next product-level milestone cannot be scored. Gate 2 was closed as superseded on 25 October (its model was already judged unusable). The open bet is a predictor of the new product chain (drive, equaliser, reverb); its training data is still being rendered, so it has no result.

technical.rationale: Since 23 October: a sealed 120-item test for the drive stage, a file that pins the song-match defaults to what the human has approved, a colour comparison on seven songs, a reverb pilot, a blind reverb estimator validated on 189 known reverbs, and a pre-registered confirmation. An overnight job has rendered 37,998 of about 40,000 chains for the product-chain predictor. Advancing is earned on tooling and on negative results that narrowed the product, not on matching quality: no new capability has been verified on real songs, and the one blind song test was negative.

breakdown.implemented: Everything in the previous report, plus: a sealed-set generator, verifier and scorer for Gate 3 (scorer not run); a blind ranking-pack builder and scorer; a dry-signal ablation driver; colour-stage builders (bounded equaliser fit, reverb candidate grid, comparison pages); a blind reverb estimator; the approved-methods file with a pinning test; and the product-chain render, training and seven-song table job (running).
breakdown.integrated: Still hand-run scripts: separation, a rebuilt clean guitar, a drive search and optional knob fine-tune, with the colour stage built as separate pilots. The estimator, the colour stage and the chain predictor are in no matcher. Nothing is one command, and nothing verifies on the pedal automatically.
breakdown.tested: Unit tests for each new module (reverb estimator 10, Gate 3 set, ranking pack, approved-methods pinning, colour, product chain). The estimator was validated on 189 known reverbs made in Helix Native; the reverb pilot and its confirmation were pre-registered and ranked blind by one listener.
breakdown.verified: On Helix Native renders only: the estimator on known reverbs (decay ordering 36 of 40 triples, mix always monotone), the human's ranking consistency in the reverb pilot (mean rank difference 0.33 against 2.67 by chance), and a null result for four candidate reverb signals. By ear: one negative blind session on drive-only matches, open preference for a light reverb on seven songs, one blind pack favouring the fitted equaliser on Mother. No real pedal has been matched, and nothing was scored against a bar the human approved.
breakdown.unfinished: Gate 3 bars (proposed, not approved) and any scoring of the sealed set; the product-chain predictor result (training not started); a reverb model; scoring of the stem-validation pack and the dry-ablation packs; a blind listen of the colour stage; matching on a real pedal; anything beyond macOS.

readiness.rationale: At the low end of Prototype. A script turns a separated song into a rebuilt clean guitar, finds a drive effect and its knobs, and writes a preset that plays on the Stomp, and bolt-on pilots show a light reverb and a fitted equaliser can be built. But the one blind listening of the drive-only matches was negative, so the demonstration is weaker than the open listens suggested. It is not Integrated: the steps are hand-run, the colour stage and the chain predictor are in no matcher, the reverb has no model, and the pedal check is manual. It is not Validated: no gate has been scored on a bar the human approved.
readiness.blocker_to_next: Integrated needs the product chain (drive, equaliser, reverb) predicted together from a song, run from one command, with the preset checked on the pedal. Today the drive match was rated badly blind, the reverb has no model and the chain predictor has no result. Validated also needs the Gate 3 bars approved, the sealed set scored once, and a blind listen that goes the right way.

summary: The goal is a tool that turns a song into an HX Stomp preset that sounds like the recorded guitar. This week the first blind listening on real songs came back negative: the human said the drive-only matches were so poor they could not even be compared, although earlier open listens called them pretty good. The human then narrowed the product to a drive effect, an equaliser and a light reverb, with no amp, cabinet or delay. A light reverb is preferred by ear, but nothing measured from the recording picks it reliably: one song confirmed a reverb estimator and one did not. A sealed blind test for the drive stage exists, but its pass bars await the human's ruling. An overnight job is rendering training data for a chain predictor and has no result yet.

biggest_problem.why: The product promises a preset that sounds like the recorded guitar, and the first blind listening on real songs said the current drive-only matches do not. Reverb, the next stage the human wants, has no usable signal either. Until a model tied to what the human hears beats a sealed baseline and passes a blind listen, the tool cannot know whether a candidate is closer, so more search or tuning would be steering by an instrument the ear has not validated. The open bet is a predictor trained on drive, equaliser and reverb chains; it is still rendering its data.

ear_qualifier: open listening, one negative blind session

Gate 1.goal: Prove both sound engines can be driven by code, and that a generated preset loads on the pedal.
criteria_plain: Helix Native renders a test clip from code (smoke test passes).
The HX Stomp renders the same test clip from code on at least one operating system.
A generated preset file is accepted by HX Edit and loads on the pedal.
The shared engine interface is frozen and the control routes are documented.
Gate 1.demonstrated: All four criteria are evidenced and the owner signed off on 2026-10-14. Caveats the owner accepted: the pedal result rested on one operating system and firmware 3.50 (the pedal has since been updated to 3.80 and its smoke test passes there); the pedal-load result was reported by the owner, not observed by an automated test.
Gate 1.remaining: Nothing for the gate itself. Windows and Linux pedal control remain unverified.
Gate 1.next_action: None. The pedal is now on firmware 3.80 and its smoke test passes there; the remaining 3.80 re-checks (parity with Native) belong to the next gate.

Gate 2.goal: Show the tool can recover a known answer: given audio made from a preset we already know, its comparison measure picks the true preset and its search finds the right blocks and settings, at thresholds agreed in advance.
criteria_plain: On the known-answer set, the tone-comparison measure ranks the true preset first at the agreed threshold.
Block types, amp and effect models, and parameter values are identified within the agreed accuracy.
A curve showing how accuracy falls as guitar separation gets worse has been recorded.
Gate 2.demonstrated: Attempt 3 ran on all 96 sealed synthetic-v3 items (ledger 2026-10-18T15:46:15): all 7 checks met on paper. Category 0.885 (bar 0.85), model 0.771 (bar 0.60), settings error 0.101 (bar 0.15), ranking the true preset first 0.979, 94 of 96 (bar 0.95), model against the random walk +0.208, settings against the random walk -0.083. The ranking check used the owner's extended rule B, amended before the run; attempts 1 and 2 keep their old-rule figures. The separation stress curve is ticked from 2026-10-16. The human's verdict the same day (DECISIONS 2026-10-18 model and method decisions): 'the model we created is garbage. Something is flawed in our testing and/or our methodology'; every lead-made method ruling behind the gate, including the admitted score and the pass claim, is treated as unapproved until the human reviews it. Still open: the confirmation run on a fresh sealed set with the attempt-3 configuration unchanged (T152) and the harness sanity checks (T155). The independent audit adds that the admitted score changed between attempts, the model bar of 0.60 sits at the random-walk level, and the result holds only when the clean recording is known. Evidence class A on paper; disowned in substance. Closed as superseded by the human on 2026-10-25 (bundle approval of the lead's decision 9; the 2026-10-18 verdict stands; the confirmation run and harness checks were cancelled). The checklist is kept as a record and is not a pass.
Gate 2.remaining: Nothing: the gate is closed, not passed. The sign-off line stays unticked.

Gate 3.goal: Show that the tool can name the right block and settings from the rendered output alone, without ever seeing the dry guitar track that made it.
criteria_plain: A sealed set of single-block items exists: random model, random settings, rendered in Native from a random held-out guitar sample the matcher never sees.

The pass bars and baselines are registered before the run, under the same no-dry-track condition. They were written down before the set was drawn but are proposed by benchmark, not approved by the human.
Blind prediction meets the bars and beats every baseline on the sealed set.
A short blind listen of the prediction re-rendered from the held-out dry sample agrees.
Gate 3.demonstrated: One of four criteria evidenced. The sealed set gate3-v1 exists: 120 single drive-block items (60 product drive models x 2 random settings) played from the reserved third guitarist's clean recordings, seed 223001, hashes recorded, labels unread, verifier re-checks every file. The bars (G3-1 to G3-5) were written down before the draw; the human has not ruled on them and nothing has been scored. Earlier informal groundwork stays evidence class D (predictor-first drive matcher on 48 blind Helix drive targets, set drawn after the method was built, no bar).
Gate 3.remaining: The human rules on the bars; one frozen method is scored once on the sealed set against the baselines; then the short blind listen (at least 30 decided trials, 6 repeats). The method to score is the chain predictor, which has no result yet.
Gate 3.blocking: The human has not ruled on the bars. Scoring allows one attempt per frozen method, and the method that would be scored (the chain predictor) is still being trained. Limit: the 120 items share about 31 distinct playing windows.
Gate 3.next_action: Human: rule on the bars. Then the lead launches one scoring run of a frozen method.

Gate 4.goal: Show that the tool can match clean recordings of real guitar pedals, judged by re-rendering the matched preset from a held-out dry take and by a short blind listen.
criteria_plain: A dry reference of the player's guitar (random playing) has been captured; it is the only dry signal the matcher may use.
A set of single real pedals (one per available category, several random settings each) has been recorded, with the matching dry take kept aside for scoring.
The matched presets meet a quality bar set before the run, and a short blind listen agrees.
Two- and three-pedal chains have been recorded and matched by the chain builder at the same bar.
Gate 4.demonstrated: Nothing yet on real pedals. Groundwork that carries over: the guitar calibration recorder and profile (one guitar), the dry-track rebuild, and a measured-pedal mode that is built and simulated only (model 96 percent in simulation); it has never been run on a pedal.
Gate 4.remaining: Capture the dry reference and the single-pedal set, choose the quality bar before the run, then record and match two- and three-pedal chains. The matcher must work without a lined-up dry take (note-invariant comparison terms, a learned guitar embedding, a phase-insensitive modulation score).
Gate 4.blocking: Depends on Gate 3 and on the player recording the pedals.
Gate 4.next_action: Wait for Gate 3; the player can plan which real distortion pedals to record.

Gate 5.goal: Show that, for real songs, the tool's preset beats the nearest ready-made community preset in blind listening.
criteria_plain: In blind listening on a 20-song set, the matched preset is preferred over the nearest community preset on most songs.
The difference between the pedal and Native on firmware 3.80 has been recorded.
Native-mode and pedal-mode matching have been compared on the same songs.
Gate 5.demonstrated: Seven songs were matched with drive blocks and heard once, openly, with no alternative candidate (evidence class C: not blind, one listener, no community-preset comparison). Pedal-versus-Native agreement on firmware 3.80 is recorded (ticked). The Native-versus-pedal comparison on songs has not been run.
Gate 5.remaining: Gate 2, the chain builder on a real engine, the pedal verification fixes, the 20-song set, blind sessions, and the Native-versus-pedal comparison on songs. A full-library test is not planned (human decision).
Gate 5.blocking: Depends on Gate 4, on the chain builder, on the pedal fixes, and on song selection.
Gate 5.next_action: Wait for Gate 4. A blind check of the seven matches (see actions) is a useful early read.

issues.title: Nothing measured from the recording reliably sets the drive knobs, and the first blind test of drive-only matches was negative
issues.problem: On 25 October the human heard, blind, the five best drive candidates for each of five songs against the separated guitar and said 'only 23 comes even close. That was pretty bad all around', then 'it's so bad I can't even compare them'. This is the first blind listening on real songs and it is negative (evidence class C as recorded by the lead: heard blind, answered aloud, not scored). It contradicts the open listen of 22 October that called the seven matches 'pretty good'. The dry-signal ablation then showed the winning drive model barely depends on the clean guitar fed to the search: against the plain rebuild, 5 to 6 of 7 songs keep the same model under each alternative input, one song changes model in every arm, and the distances are not comparable across inputs. The listening measure that ranks the candidates (AFx-Rep) has no ear validation against a separated guitar, and its validation session produced a verdict instead of ranks.
issues.impact: A drive-only match cannot be shown to beat anything the human would accept, and the ranking and knobs rest on a measure the ear has not validated on real songs. Without a signal that tracks what the human hears, neither search nor prediction can be tuned toward a better answer.
issues.cause: Not established. Candidates named in the notes: one drive effect standing in for a whole rig (the human has since moved to drive, equaliser and reverb), the rebuilt clean guitar being an approximation, the separated stem carrying leftovers from other instruments, and the measure not tracking the ear on real songs. None was isolated.
issues.resolution: Predict the product chain with a model trained on chain-rendered audio and judge it against the sealed set and a blind listen, with bars the human approves first; rate the built dry-ablation packs; treat the stem verdict as a standing negative until a blind session goes the other way.
issues.owner: learning (the chain predictor, running); benchmark scores once the human approves the bars; the human rates the dry-ablation packs
issues.next_step: Read the chain predictor when training ends; the human rates the dry-ablation packs and rules on the Gate 3 bars.

issues.title: Reverb has no model: nothing measured from the recording agrees with the listener, and a real tail is readable on only 2 of 7 stems
issues.problem: The human rejected a fixed reverb default and asked for a model. The pre-registered pilot (27 reverb candidates per song, blind ranks on six songs, the listener consistent: mean rank difference 0.33 against 2.67 by chance) found no agreement from any computable signal: the listening measure 0.05, tail statistics 0.04, the time-based regressors -0.09, dip fill -0.40 (opposite sign). A blind estimator built afterwards is accurate on known reverbs (decay ordering 36 of 40 triples, rank correlation 0.85 to 0.89 on five songs; mix 0.88 to 0.94) but cannot tell Room from Plate from Hall (43 percent against 33 by chance), and on the real stems it reads a real tail on only 2 of 7 (Mother 0.70 s, Territorial 0.90 s); the other five read the separator's leftover. The pre-registered confirmation held on Mother (named closest ranked 1 of 7, named furthest 7 of 7) and was not reproducible on Territorial (the human's repeat got ranks 4 and 1), so pooled it did not confirm.
issues.impact: The product chain needs a reverb per song. The only evidence that reverb helps is open listening (a light reverb preferred on all seven songs); type and amount cannot be chosen from the stem on 5 of 7 songs, and Plate, the open favourite, was not preferred in the blind ranks (mean rank Room 3.9, Hall 4.0, Plate 4.4; ties frequent).
issues.cause: Known in part: separator leftovers hide the tail on 5 of 7 stems and the human said not to work on the separator; the shared low and high cuts remove most of what tells reverb types apart; some clips are hard to rank (Territorial repeat inconsistent; the Cherub Rock section was unsuitable).
issues.resolution: The human rules on 'estimate when readable, fall back otherwise'; the overnight reverb heads are compared with the estimator on the seven songs; more songs are ranked blind with the estimator's pick named in advance.
issues.owner: tone-metrics (estimator); learning (reverb heads); the human rules on the model and ranks more songs
issues.next_step: Human: rule on the reverb model and choose another Cherub Rock section (see the action list).

issues.title: The product-chain predictor is the open bet, and single-block predictors do not transfer to chains
issues.problem: The human set the product chain to drive, equaliser, reverb (no amp, cabinet or delay). The predictors built for other slots were trained on single blocks and fail inside chains: inside a finished chain the drive is named right 2 times in 100 and the amp 1 in 100, against 93 and 54 alone. A small chain-trained pilot reached 18 percent top-3 on the drive (chance 6). A larger job is rendering now: about 40,000 drive, optional equaliser and optional reverb chains, 15 percent from the human's own session recordings. At 2026-10-26 16:23 local it had 37,998 chains done (shard 96 of 105, 2 dropped); rendering stops by 20:00, then training. No result, no ledger row, nothing adopted.
issues.impact: Until a chain predictor works, every song match is a single drive effect and the product cannot be called integrated. If the larger run also fails, the plan for predicting a chain needs a different method.
issues.cause: Predictors and search were built drive first, and single-block data came before the chain check. Inside a chain, anything in front of a block hurts its predictor and a cabinet after it nearly erases it.
issues.resolution: Read the new heads against held-out library files, the held-out part of the human's session and the seven songs; then, once the bars are approved, against the sealed Gate 3 set; the human hears any adopted match blind.
issues.owner: learning runs the job; benchmark scores; the human approves the method
issues.next_step: Let the render and training finish, then read the seven-song table.

issues.title: Gate 3 bars are proposed, not approved, so the sealed test cannot be scored
issues.problem: A sealed test set exists: 120 single drive-block items rendered from the reserved third guitarist's recordings, hashes recorded, labels unread. Benchmark wrote the pass bars down before drawing it: right model first at least 0.50 and in the top three at least 0.70; Drive knob within 0.15 on at least 0.60 of right-model items (and 0.50 across the other free knobs); each bar beating every baseline by 0.15 or more (paired, exact test p below 0.05); then a short blind listen with at least 30 decided trials where the prediction wins at least 70 percent. The human has not ruled on any of them.
issues.impact: The only product-level milestone cannot be scored, and the overnight predictor's numbers, when they arrive, will not count toward the gate. A set allows one scoring attempt per frozen method.
issues.cause: Waiting on a human ruling (standing rule: pass bars need the human's approval before they take effect). A limit to weigh: the 120 items share about 31 non-overlapping 10-second windows of playing, so the effective sample is nearer 30 to 40 than 120.
issues.resolution: The human approves, changes or rejects each bar; the lead records it in the human's words; benchmark scores once.
issues.owner: the human rules; benchmark scores after the lead launches the run
issues.next_step: Human: rule on the Gate 3 bars (see the action list).

issues.title: The effect-slot predictors are trained, not verified: weak on a new guitarist and failing inside chains
issues.problem: On held-out recordings of players seen in training (18 files from the two library players; the many test clips are cut from those files, so the effective sample is 18, not thousands) the predictors name the exact model about 54 percent of the time for amps (224 models), 76 percent for cabinets, 56 percent for delays, 75 percent for modulation, 47 percent for reverb and 82 percent for equalisers. On a player held out of training the same predictors drop to roughly 19 to 31 percent (amp), 32 to 35 (cabinet), 25 to 32 (delay), 47 to 60 (modulation), 31 to 39 (reverb) and 49 to 67 (equaliser). Inside a finished chain they fall to near chance. Knob accuracy is modest, and the 'constant mid-range guess scores about 0.3' baseline it is compared with was not re-measured. Scope note: the amp, cabinet, modulation and delay slots are out of scope while the product chain is drive, equaliser and reverb (human, 2026-10-25), so these numbers matter again only if the chain is widened.
issues.impact: The human is a new player to these predictors, and so is any later user, and the product matches chains. As they stand, the slot predictors cannot shortlist anything in a chain matcher.
issues.cause: Only two library guitarists and one session of the human's playing exist in the training pool. Drive showed the same gap until the 150,000-render dataset added more guitar variety (new-player model accuracy 33 to 47 percent became 62 to 75).
issues.resolution: Train on chain-rendered audio first (the pilot), then add guitar variety: the human's calibrated notes, and another licensed library if one can be found. Re-measure with the same held-out-player split and on the chain test set.
issues.owner: learning builds the data; the human decides which guitar material to add
issues.next_step: Read the chain training pilot; then propose which guitars to add and the render budget.

issues.title: No pedal measurement counts until the sampling defects are handled
issues.problem: The pedal verification found real defects: the audio stream over USB is not stable for about 0.7 s after it starts, amps carry sound over from the previous render, the pedal refuses four effect models in whole-preset writes, and some delay and reverb settings glide slowly when changed in place. Setting truth passed 20 of 40 items, repeatability 12 of 17. A longer pre-roll fixed the first problem, but a one-sample slip still happens about once in 90 renders. The human confirmed the pedal's blocks are editable after sessions.
issues.impact: The pedal is the final judge of the preset. Until the slip is detected or re-taken, pedal numbers cannot be used as evidence, and earlier pedal agreement figures are understated in noise. Gate 2 (Native only) is not affected; Gate 5 is.
issues.cause: Known for each defect (stream start-up, amp state, device refusals, parameter glide). The remaining slip has no recorded cause.
issues.resolution: Detect and re-take slipped renders, find why four models are refused, measure or avoid the parameter glide, then re-register the pedal rules (float32 read-back, an absolute -60 dB settle criterion, floors from rested renders) and re-run.
issues.owner: stomp-engine; the lead schedules the re-run
issues.next_step: Detect or re-take slipped renders, then fix the refusals and the glide.

issues.title: The rebuilt clean guitar barely changes which drive wins, and nothing says it improves the match
issues.problem: Songs have no clean guitar, so the matcher rebuilds one from transcribed notes. The dry-signal ablation (4 arms per song plus a level-only arm, 30 searches) found the winning drive model mostly unchanged by the input: against the plain rebuild, the envelope-imposed rebuild kept the model on 6 of 7 songs, the library clean guitar and the level-only arm on 5 of 7; DS-Sample changed in every arm and Satisfaction's plain pick is a dead tie. The distances are from different dry tracks and are not comparable, so they say nothing about which input is closer. The seven blind packs are built and unrated. The level convention is settled provisionally at the play-along level (-28.1 dBFS; bundle approval, 25 October).
issues.impact: Either the rebuild adds little to the pick, or the measure cannot see its effect; the ear on the unrated packs is the only way to tell. Until then the rebuild and the calibration cannot be credited with a gain.
issues.cause: Level and the drive amount are entangled, the rebuild ablation (same search, generic library clean guitar) was never run, and the calibrated run changed three things at once.
issues.resolution: The human rates the seven dry-ablation packs (blind, sealed keys) before reading the picks table.
issues.owner: the human rates; dry-signal reads the result

issues.title: Blind evidence on real songs is one negative session, and the listener's consistency is mixed
issues.problem: The seven song matches and their fine-tunes were heard once, openly. The first blind listening on real songs (25 October) was negative, but it was answered aloud and not scored, so there is no agreement number for the listening measure. The listener was very consistent on the reverb pilot (mean rank difference 0.33 against 2.67 by chance, 6 of 6 within 1) and mixed on the confirmation (Mother within 1, Territorial not reproducible); across the earlier pair sessions the human's repeats agreed 7 of 12 times. The one gate run that was blind, sealed and pre-registered (Gate 2) was disowned by the human and is now closed as superseded. The score the lead admitted for the known-recording case is unapproved and at chance on hard same-performance pairs (10 of 25).
issues.impact: The ear is the final judge, and an open listen can flatter a method. Every 'closer', 'same or better' and 'pretty good' in this report is directional, not a result; method choices made on those numbers (fine-tuning, calibration, chord lists) are not yet defensible.
issues.cause: Blind sessions take preparation and the quick open listens were what the human asked for; meanwhile test settings became defaults by reuse (the final ranking by the listening measure, knob fine-tuning with the level knobs free) without an itemised approval, which the lead has acknowledged as its failure.
issues.resolution: Run the blind validation of the listening measure against separated guitars (5 songs by 5 candidates on the same rebuilt dry, ranked blind with repeats; report rank agreement); ablate fine-tuning and calibration blind, one factor at a time; carry at least 6 repeats per session and report the listener's consistency first; seal Gate 3 with bars before the chain pilot is read; record approvals one line per item.
issues.owner: the human decides the design (decisions 2, 3, 6, 8); the lead prepares the packs; benchmark registers bars
issues.next_step: Score the stem-validation pack if the human wants the agreement number; rate the dry-ablation packs; carry at least 6 repeats per session and report the listener's consistency first.

issues.title: Delay is the weakest effect: 5 of 12 exact models on the sealed set
issues.problem: On Gate 2 attempt 3 (96 sealed items; all seven checks met on paper, but the human judged the model unusable and the gate is unsigned) the exact model was right on cab 12, eq 11, reverb 11, mod 10, comp 10, amp 8, drive 7 and delay 5 of 12. The seven delay misses: four named another delay model (i001, i049, i073, i089), three a different kind of effect (i041 a compressor, i065 and i081 an equaliser). Two ranking misses (i039, i095) are cabinets.
issues.impact: Gate 2's checklist is not what blocks it now, but delay is common in real tones and the model is wrong on more than half of the delay items. Real songs will be harder than this known-clean-recording test.
issues.cause: Not yet diagnosed. Swell-type and ducked delays look similar to other delays at the settings drawn; v3 is now seen, so diagnosis must use the development sets.
issues.resolution: Diagnose the delay misses on development data (echo time, feedback and mix versus model), then strengthen the time-based specialist; listen to the delay misses to see whether the swaps matter by ear.
issues.owner: search builds the delay work; the human listens; the lead schedules
issues.next_step: None: delay is on hold (human, 2026-10-25: 'I don't think any of the songs have any delay in them').

issues.title: Guitar separation quality on real songs is unknown
issues.problem: Guitar separation has been scored only on artificial mixes: quality falls from 21.2 dB (guitar alone) to 7.3 dB with a second guitar in the mix. No real song has a quality score. Update 2026-10-23: seven real songs have been separated and heard, and the human compared each match with the separated guitar, but no separation quality number exists for real songs, and one stem lost about 20 dB of bass. Update 2026-10-25: the human said not to work on the separator ('The extracted samples are just fine'); the reverb estimator shows five of seven stems hide the tail under separator leftovers.
issues.impact: If the isolated guitar on a real song contains drums, vocals or artefacts, the tone comparison will chase those instead of the guitar and Gate 5 results will be unreliable.
issues.cause: No real-song stress set exists, and the only separation model aimed at guitar has no stated licence so it was not used.
issues.resolution: Run the separation stress test on a few real songs, locally, and record how accuracy falls as the mix gets denser.
issues.owner: separation, after the owner supplies songs
issues.next_step: None: no separator work (human, 2026-10-25). Real-song separation quality stays unmeasured.

issues.title: Building whole chains from single blocks is not yet shown to work
issues.problem: Single blocks are matched first and whole chains are built from analysis: the kinds of block present, ordered by common patterns. The pattern prior now rests on 2,068 curated presets and shows strong order rules. But the block-presence detector passed its test only for the cabinet and for whether a gain stage is present; for delay, reverb and modulation it missed its bars. The chain builder exists and is tested only with fake engines.
issues.impact: Gate 5 (real songs) needs whole chains. Presence is used only as a soft hint, so every time-based block must be confirmed by rendering with and without it.
issues.cause: Behind an amp and cabinet, single-block detectors call the extra block a drive almost every time; comparing against the clean recording cannot isolate a block that follows a non-linear amp.
issues.resolution: Judge post-amp blocks against the chain's current best render, render a multi-block test set on Native, and run the chain builder on a real engine. Cabinet choice by deconvolution looks promising.
issues.next_step: None now: the product chain is drive, equaliser, reverb and the chain builder is out of scope until the chain widens.

issues.title: The pedal and Native disagree on one cabinet setting
issues.problem: The cabinet's Early Reflections setting does not sound the same on the pedal and in Native.
issues.impact: A preset found on the fast Native engine can sound different on the real pedal. At the value the search chose, the two engines' recordings cancel by only 3.6 dB (poor agreement); with the setting at 0 they cancel by 31 dB (close agreement).
issues.cause: Not yet known. Candidates are an older algorithm in the pedal, a different parameter scale, or a delay-structure difference. Other parameters tested at their extremes agreed.
issues.resolution: Find the cause, or measure every searchable parameter on both engines and let the search free only the parameters that agree.
issues.owner: native-engine and stomp-engine; benchmark for the per-parameter audit
issues.next_step: Keep the setting at 0 for pedal presets and let the pedal check it (the accepted rule); the verification suites cover settings generally.

issues.title: Native verification leaves recorded misses that are explained, not fixed
issues.problem: After three engine fixes (baked controls no longer sent, hosts that start in the other numeric mode are re-prepared, a state latch from the first amp loaded), repeatability is 216 of 216 and nothing unexplained remains. Two rules still miss as written: setting truth 116 of 120 and baked values 63 of 73. issues.impact: None blocks Gate 2 (ruled acceptable on 2026-10-17). Native results produced before the fixes were made by the earlier engine and may differ by rounding up to about -21 dB on a few chains.

issues.title: The software engine cannot stand in for every pedal effect
issues.problem: Measurements show Native can stand in for the pedal on amps, cabinets, dynamics, equalisers, most drives, delays, Room, Plate, Spring and Chamber reverbs, Hall above 500 Hz, and the modulation effects. recent_changes.text: Gate 2 attempt 3 met all 7 checks on the 96 sealed items: category 0.885, model 0.771, settings error 0.101, ranking the true preset first 0.979 under the owner's extended rule, better than the random walk on model and settings. The gate is not passed until the owner signs. Delay (5 of 12 exact models) is now the weakest effect. The same day the human judged the model 'garbage' and declared every lead-made method ruling behind it unapproved; the confirmation run and harness checks stay open.

Gate 2 attempt 2 did not pass: 6 of 7 checks on the 96 sealed items. Category 0.865 (was 0.802), model 0.760 (was 0.646), settings error 0.091, better than the random walk on both model and settings, consistency split passes. Ranking the true preset first fails at 0.9375 against 0.95 (was 0.990): six misses on amp, drive and one cabinet, which the middle baseline shares. Modulation and drive are weakest; cabinet and equaliser are perfect. The rule is unchanged and v2 is now seen.

The human approved the next improvement round for Gate 2 attempt 3: a gain-stage score term, drive and modulation specialists, and a fresh sealed synthetic-v3 (generated and sealed since). Synthetic-v2 is now spent: diagnosis only, never used to admit a change.

Specialists were adopted for four families: cabinet and equaliser (model 24 of 24 on development items against 18 of 24 for the general method), time-based effects (held-out model 14 to 19), amp (param error 0.224 to 0.120), and a dispatcher plus adapters that route each family to its specialist. Gate 2 attempt 2 ran on all of them; category and model rose accordingly.

Parallel jobs now survive restarts (an item-level queue, workers grow and shrink with the host scaler), the Native host cap was raised from 6 to 8 on the human's instruction, and a false silence alarm on a very quiet true preset (item i062) was fixed; i062 stays in the set as a normal item.

Gate 2 attempt 1 did not pass. On all 96 items: model 0.646, settings error 0.132, ranking 0.990 and settings better than the random walk pass; category 0.802 (bar 0.85) and model non-inferiority to the random walk (low end -0.083, needs -0.05) fail. The 80 untuned items agree. Strong families: drive, cabinet, compressor, delay; weak: modulation, reverb, amp. The next attempt uses a fresh set and per-family specialists.

The human directed a specialist per effect family, with single blocks first and chains built from analysis, no full-library test, trained weights may be published, and the cabinet-response library may be used for training. The 19 non-impulse-response recordings were removed from the library folder to the Trash. The pass rule was frozen before the run, and the baseline "random search" is now called the random walk.

Native is verified for Gate 2: three engine bugs were fixed (baked controls, hosts in the other rounding mode, an amp state latch), repeatability is 216 of 216, nothing is unexplained, and an in-run sentinel now guards long jobs. Recorded misses (116 of 120 setting-truth pairs, 63 of 73 baked renders) are one-step rounding and input/output blocks.

The pedal verification found real sampling defects: unstable USB audio for about 0.7 s after start, amp state carried between renders, four models refused, and a slow in-place glide on some delay and reverb settings. A longer pre-roll fixed the first; a one-sample slip remains in about 1 render in 90. No pedal result counts until it is handled.

Search got measured seeding (the target's own delay time, reverb decay and modulation rate set the starting point) and then a hybrid method with broad draws, narrowing and refinement, chosen by a rule fixed before the last run. On the 16 development items model accuracy went from 6 to 13 of 16 over the day (development only, not gate evidence).
Baselines were recorded: the middle-of-every-knob guess and the random walk. The random walk scores high because it has 300 tries over a 47-model pool judged by the trusted score.

The curated preset corpus (2,068 presets after cleaning) gave strong order rules, super-groups and heavy concentration of model use; descriptive metadata adds little. Only category-level statistics are committed.

The cabinet impulse-response library analysis shows that estimating a cabinet by deconvolution is promising: the pedal's cabinet is the top match in 22 of 24 real-clip tests when the amp is right. It is useless with the wrong amp. No library data leaves the machine.

The block-presence detector, scored once on its test split, passed only for the cabinet and for whether a gain stage is present. It is used as a soft hint only; time-based blocks are confirmed by rendering with and without them.

A chain builder (tested with fake engines) and a blind A/B listening tool were built, and a local Gate 2 explainer for a non-technical reader was added (kept off the public repository). None of these changes a gate on its own.

The two engine items that were held back (out-of-range values and a real-guitar smoke test) are done: the real-guitar smoke test passes on Native. On-demand capture defaults off after it opened an editor window per preset.
Model choice tied the old pool pass at 7 of 16 development models under the old provisional score. This was superseded on 2026-10-17: the baselines are now recorded and the hybrid search replaced it.

The Native verification suite first showed one of 216 repeat renders at -97.4 dB against the -100 dB line. The cause was a state carried between models (an amp latch), plus baked controls and a rounding mode. After three engine fixes repeatability is 216 of 216 (worst -161.5 dB), with an in-run sentinel in place.

Native block fingerprints were measured for 602 of 605 library models (24 of about 3,600 settings were silent, all expected), and rendering many candidates at once is 1.46 times faster than one at a time with identical results. Model choice per slot is built.

The pedal's two-variant pass equals serial renders on firmware 3.80 and is about 1.7 times faster per variant (1.70 s against about 2.9 s). This closes the audio check that was open last report. Pedal restores are now judged by decoded equality, since raw bytes can differ by 3 after the pedal re-encodes.

A chain-pattern prior was built from 129 presets: drive comes before amp in 55 of 55 presets with both, amp before cab 90 of 90, delay before reverb in 96 percent. It is aggregate statistics only; no preset content is committed. It is not yet used by a chain builder.

New direction from the human: single blocks first, with chains built from analysis of real presets (which kinds of block are present, ordered by common patterns). The curated preset and cabinet-IR libraries stay local and are never committed; the song-metadata lookup (artist and title only) is approved as opt-in.

The human chose the Gate 2 scoring rules (tune the measure for the known-recording case; count identical-sounding look-alikes as ties) and waived the 'right chain structure' target for Gate 2, which now covers single blocks only. Chain structure moves to Gate 4. Scoring rules 2 and 3 are coded.

The tone comparison was admitted for single blocks when the clean recording is known. Tuned on a train split and scored once on a held-out split of 96 items, it ranked the true preset first 0.990 of the time against a bar of 0.90 (older measure 0.781), counting identical-sounding look-alikes as ties. The tuning score matched the test score, so it was not overfit. This replaces the failed first check as the main evidence for that case only. Update 2026-10-18: the human judged the resulting model unusable and the admission is unapproved; in blind rating on hard same-performance pairs the measure agreed with the ear 10 of 25 times (chance).

The first trust check on real Helix sound failed: no tone-comparison measure picks the true preset reliably. On new notes the best managed about 7 times in 40 against a bar of 36; the measures react more to the notes played than to the tone. With the same notes and a lined-up recording one measure reached 0.725 (0.875 if look-alikes that sound identical are ignored). This replaces the earlier stand-in result as the main evidence and is now the biggest problem.

The software engine now holds 605 of the pedal's 607 effect models as single-block templates (the other 2 are refused by Native). Every template was replayed in a fresh host. This opens model choice from a library, but the blocks are not yet measured.

Delay times in the software engine now move in 10 ms steps instead of 63 ms, because Native honours a narrower control range. Block Level was also given a finer range (0.25 dB steps with 0 dB on the grid).

The measurements settled where the software engine can stand in for the pedal: amps, cabinets, dynamics, equalisers, most drives, delays, four reverb types, Hall above 500 Hz and the modulation effects. The pedal still checks Ganymede-type reverbs, Hall on bass-heavy material, Bitcrusher-type drives and Early Reflections. A suggested delay-time correction of under 1 in 100 was rejected: the apparent error was Native's control step, not an engine difference.

Two chains in one pedal pass give the same sound as one chain per pass on firmware 3.80, and code to render two chains per pass was written. Its audio comparison has not run because the Mac's audio failed during the session. Update: the audio comparison was later run and passed (see the 2026-10-16 entry on the pedal's two-variant pass).
The separation stress curve is recorded on a synthetic mix: guitar-only quality 21.2 dB falls to 7.3 dB with a second guitar. This ticks one Gate 2 item but says nothing yet about real songs.

The known-answer harness (96 one-block presets) was built and a 3-item run made. The run is provisional and not gate evidence; its first version scored the true preset against itself and was voided and re-run.

The search keeps scoring the full clip: shorter clips did worse in the clip-length study. Two-chain passes on Native are out of scope (decided by the owner), and time-variant blocks are opt-in for search.

Pedal engine work: a shared pedal lock with a device check, layout-changing loads written whole with read-back, and the Simple Delay Scale report explained (not a fault). A pedal session had control steps pass but audio fail (Mac audio down); the pedal was restored. These are not yet committed.

The pedal's blocks no longer stay locked after a control session. The helper now ends each session the way the pedal's own editing program does; a person confirmed the blocks were editable afterwards on firmware 3.80, where the lock had still occurred before the fix.

The pedal now runs firmware 3.80. Its engine smoke test passes there, and 9 of 9 whole-preset writes (including amps with impulse-response cabinets and one block from each effect category) landed and the pedal was restored byte for byte. Pedal-versus-Native agreement has not yet been re-measured on 3.80.
Gate 1 was signed off: both engines are driven by code and a generated preset loads on the pedal.
Helix Native now loads new sounds without a person at the keyboard and renders about seven times faster, and it stopped running out of memory.
The pedal write is now checked parameter by parameter. This traced and fixed a bug that made a delay run far too wet when the owner played a preset live on the pedal.
A first real song section was matched end to end and loaded on the pedal. The result was informal progress, not a validation.
Rendering a chain one block at a time matched rendering it whole on a test chain, which opens the way to measuring blocks individually.
A new problem was found: one cabinet setting sounds different on the pedal and in Native. Presets for the pedal keep it at 0 for now.
The first real-song run showed the tone score is not reliable: its top two candidates were almost tied and the listener preferred one clearly.
A silent bug that could reuse an outdated Native setup (and made one measurement look much worse than it was) was found and fixed; the false result was voided.

Two extra tone-comparison measures were added (a sharper loudness-shape measure and a learned audio embedding). Neither came close to the target on stand-in signals, so they did not move Gate 2 forward.
The block measuring kit was finished offline. It has not touched Helix yet, so it does not advance readiness until it is run.
The owner approved the per-block approach (measure and search block by block). It adds work before Gate 2 but shrinks the search space.

Checking candidates on the pedal got much faster: a search trial went from 10.9 s to 3.8 s and the per-test session overhead from 3.81 s to 0.77 s. A verification finalist improved less, from 29.2 s to 24.7 s. The search now uses these options by default (task T062), but how much that speeds a real search has not yet been timed on the pedal. These timings are on one pedal with one chain type; they say nothing about match quality.

Helix Native's speed work (T055) is finished. Capturing a new chain fell from about 31 s to 1.2 s in one session and 0.39 s with three sessions (216 blocks in 84.6 s). A pool of 6 parallel hosts runs 9.9 two-second tests per second (4.6 on ten-second clips); 10 hosts did a little better but with memory pressure and swapping, so the cap is 6. Bypass by MIDI control still matches separate captures (-328.7 dB), and a fault where about 1 host in 10 rendered differently is now caught by a start-up check. Measured on one Mac; nothing here has been judged by ear.

Follow-up Native work (T064): the two template sets used for matching (B and B0) were re-captured with Hum and Ripple at 0, so the matcher has all 7 test candidates under both engine policies. A scan of 607 pedal block models found only 2 that Native 3.82 refuses to load, so nearly the whole catalog can be captured for Native; the library itself is still not captured.

The pedal's two-path layout difference is fixed (T063). Our two-path version of a stored preset used to cancel against the one saved by the pedal's editor at only -9.3 dB; it now cancels at -85.7 dB, the same as the editor's preset repeated against itself. Single-path loads are unchanged. Measured on firmware 3.80, one preset, one pedal.

The rule that two-path renders may only be compared with two-path renders is lifted, because after the layout fix a two-path pass matches single-chain renders (Path A -72.9 dB against a repeat floor of -68.7; Path B -52.6 against -42.7). Two chains per pass can be used for checks; the 2.0x gain was measured on firmware 3.50 and is not re-measured on 3.80.

Decided by the owner: the amp's Hum and Ripple settings are frozen at 0 on both engines. They added a free-running noise that made two renders of the same preset differ at about -30 dB (against -72 to -91 dB at 0), which hid real differences and blocked the shorter pedal waits. This closes the open question and removes it from the owner's action list.

Decided by the owner: Helix Native runs at most 6 hosts at once (measured on 32 GB of memory: green memory pressure at 6, yellow with swapping at 8 and 10). All Native pool figures in this report are for 6 hosts.

Decided by the owner: Native results from before 2026-10-16 are kept as history and not re-run wholesale. About 1 host in 10 had rendered differently and delay trims could differ by up to 30 samples. The results we rely on are re-measured in the parity spot checks and the Gate 2 benchmark.

The continuous-integration build (the automatic test run on GitHub) was fixed in commit 07b66ed: one test that needs a local-only file is skipped when the file is absent. It changes no product capability.

Overnight, training data for amp, cabinet, modulation, delay, reverb and equaliser was rendered and the predictors trained. On 18 held-out recordings from the two library players they name the exact model well (cabinet 76 percent, equaliser 82, modulation 75) and poorly on a new player (amp 19 to 31 percent). Knobs are modest. Trained, not verified; nothing is adopted into any matcher.

The amp 'silence' failures were explained (a fixed -90 dBFS render floor cut off genuinely quiet renders at low Master settings, mostly on preamps) and fixed by refilling 5,526 of 5,653 failed clips; 127 clips that are truly digital silence are left out.

Re-running the seven songs with the human's calibrated guitar lowered the listening-measure distance on 5 of 7 songs (clearly on 3). Label: listening-measure distance across different dry tracks; no ear verdict. The measure is not validated to order renders of different clean guitars, and notes, tone and level changed together, so no gain can be credited. The human wants to test the presets themselves.

The human approved a chain transfer test: about 300 random drive, amp and cabinet chains (plus optional effects) to see whether the slot predictors still name their block inside a chain. It ran the same day (see the result below).

A full drive search against a rebuilt clean guitar was run on seven songs; the human listened once, openly, side by side with the separated guitar, with no alternative candidate, and said 'those actually all sound pretty good' (evidence class C). A knob fine-tune lowered the listening-measure distance on 6 of 7 and the human heard 'the same or better' in the same open pass; Output and Master moved freely.

The human recorded a guided calibration session for their guitar. The profile (263 own notes, tone curve, normal playing level -36.1 dBFS) shows the real guitar plays 8 decibels quieter than the earlier stand-in level and is more mid-forward than the library guitars.

Basic Pitch was installed locally and its settings were swept against the human's dry takes; a clean guitar can now be rebuilt for all seven separated songs. Alignment to the stem was good on slow parts and unmeasurable on fast dense riffs.

A chord list on Mother made the match more decisive (runner-up margin 0.023 against 0.002), but the human heard the plain version as better in one open comparison, so the chord-list rebuild stays an option. The distances quoted for it (0.706 against 0.629) carry the label: listening-measure distance across different dry tracks; no ear verdict beyond that one open preference.

Five blind song matches (no dry guitar) were heard as two 'pretty off', one the closest so far, two 'somewhat close'. The weak spots are Zero Amp Bass DI standing in for a fuzz and a single drive block standing in for a rig.
The human approved a fixed slot order for chain prediction (drive, amp, cabinet, modulation, delay, reverb, equaliser, each optional) and a calibration step for each guitar before matching.
Swapping the listening measure for freely licensed alternatives (PANNs, DAC) fell short of the current one, so the current measure stays, with its licence question open.

A predictor-first drive matcher named the correct drive model first on 85 percent of 48 blind Helix targets (100 percent within three) in about 12 renders. On the human's own takes 67 and 88 percent. The human heard the first song match as pretty good. Evidence class D: the set was drawn by the search agent after the method was built, with no bar; the own-take cells are not statistically significant.

A tuned version of a tutorial amp chain beat the tutorial settings in a short blind session (8 trials, 6 decided, 1 of 2 repeats consistent; mean rating 4.0 against 2.5) and in one live listen, on one song and one window. Directional only; it does not show that a whole chain can be tuned reliably by search.

The chain transfer test answered no: on 295 finished chains the single-block predictors name the drive 2 percent and the amp 1 percent of the time (93 and 54 alone); cabinet 25, modulation 21, delay 10, reverb 28, equaliser 12 percent; knobs at a constant guess. A drive in front of the amp hurts the amp predictor and a cabinet after them nearly erases both. The 240,000 single-block renders cannot be used as chain shortlists as they are. The human approved a chain-trained pilot (about 5,000 chains, scored on the same test set), which is running.

At the human's request the lead produced a project analysis from an independent methodology audit and two research surveys. Findings the lead accepts: no result since mid-October rests on a sealed blind test; the listening measure is used beyond its ear validation; several methods became defaults by reuse without itemised approval; 240,000 single-block renders preceded the chain check; the rebuilt dry's contribution is unmeasured. Ten itemised decisions are listed for the human. This report corrects the overstatements the audit found (one experiment heard rather than two independent tests; measured-pedal mode is simulation only; 18 held-out files rather than thousands of clips; one song and six decided trials rather than 'a whole chain can be tuned'; the admitted score is unapproved and at chance on hard pairs; slot predictors trained, not verified; Gate 2 disowned by the human; every 'closer' figure labelled as a cross-dry-track distance with no ear verdict).

The first blind listening on real songs was negative. On five songs the human heard the five best drive candidates against the separated guitar and said 'so bad I can't even compare them'. It contradicts the open listens of 22 October that called the same kind of match 'pretty good'. Heard blind but answered aloud and not scored (evidence class C). Two stopped jobs (a preset-corpus render and a separation re-score) can resume.

The human refocused the product: drive, then delay or reverb, then equaliser, with no amps or cabinets for now; delay was then put on hold, so the chain is drive, equaliser, reverb. An amp may be tested only as a stand-in for the drive. Gate 2 was closed as superseded and the 'yes go' bundle approved the governance changes (recorded as provisional).

Colour pilots on three then seven songs: a light reverb after the drive was preferred on all seven (open listening), fitted equaliser variants could not be told apart (kept at the human's request), the amp stand-in was mixed, and one blind Mother pack favoured the fitted equaliser. Plate sounded best openly but was not preferred in the later blind ranks. Directional only (class C, one B).

The reverb pilot found no signal that agrees with the human: four pre-registered candidate signals all failed (best 0.05 rank correlation), although the listener was very consistent (mean rank difference 0.33 against 2.67 by chance). The human rejected a fixed reverb default and asked for a model.

A blind reverb estimator was built and validated on 189 known reverbs (decay ordering 36 of 40, mix always monotone, type not separable). On real stems it reads a tail on only 2 of 7; the rest is separator leftovers. The human said not to work on the separator.

The pre-registered confirmation of the estimator held on Mother (named closest ranked 1 of 7, furthest 7 of 7) and was not reproducible on Territorial; pooled it is not confirmed. One song is not a result.

Dry-signal ablation measured (30 searches): the winning drive model stays the same on 5 to 6 of 7 songs under each alternative clean-guitar input; DS-Sample changes in every arm. Distances are not comparable; seven blind packs are built and unrated. No readiness gain until the ear rates them.

Gate 3 advanced from 0 to 1 of 4 criteria: a sealed 120-item blind set was generated on the reserved third guitarist's recordings, with bars written down first. The bars are proposed by benchmark and not approved by the human; nothing is scored.

Defaults are now pinned to a human-approved list (a file plus a test): knob fine-tuning is an option with the level knobs locked, and the provisional loss and the drive families are no longer defaults. Bundle approvals are recorded as provisional.

An unattended overnight job started rendering about 40,000 drive, equaliser and reverb chains (15 percent from the human's own session recordings) to train the product-chain predictor. At 2026-10-26 16:23 local: 37,998 chains done, shard 96 of 105, render stops by 20:00, then training. In progress; no result.

The sealed 120-item set exists; the bars are proposed and await the human's ruling. Nothing is scored.
Estimator confirmed on one song of two; the human has not yet ruled on 'estimate when readable, fall back otherwise'.

Seven dry-ablation packs unrated; the stem-validation pack was answered with a verdict, not scored; a Cherub Rock section for reverb is needed; the calibrated presets have not been played on the Stomp.
Handle the residual one-sample slip (about 1 in 90 renders), the four refused models and the in-place glide. No pedal result counts until then.
Opt-in MusicBrainz lookups (artist and title only). A 3-song live probe found all 3, but years and tags need a second lookup.

components.name: Sound engines: Helix Native and the HX Stomp pedal
components.purpose: Turn a candidate preset and a clean guitar clip into sound, so candidates can be compared. Native is fast and offline; the pedal is the real thing.
components.works: Both engines are driven from code on macOS. Native is verified for Gate 2: exact settings apart from explained misses, 216 of 216 repeat renders, a sentinel against drift. The pedal two-variant pass, whole-preset writes and decoded-equality restores work.
components.missing: Windows and Linux, stereo blocks, the cabinet Early Reflections setting, some reverb and drive types. Pedal verification is incomplete: four refused models, a slow glide on some settings, and a one-sample slip in about 1 render in 90.
components.problem: No pedal measurement counts until the residual slip is handled.
components.next: Detect or re-take slipped pedal renders, then fix the refusals and the glide, then re-register and re-run the pedal rules.
components.confidence: Native: hardware-measured on one Mac, 9,770 renders in the verification. Pedal: hardware, firmware 3.80, with recorded failures; ear not involved.

components.name: Preset files and the block catalog
components.purpose: Read, write and validate the preset files the pedal and Native load.
components.works: Reference files round-trip exactly, models are read from the owner's own install, generated files load, and a chain-pattern prior built from 2,068 curated presets (category-level statistics only) shows strong order rules.
components.missing: Building up to three snapshots from a match, and forcing snapshot values to equal block values inside the writer.
components.problem: A stale snapshot value can silently change the sound; the rule 'block values win' is applied in scripts but not yet in the writer.
components.next: Move the snapshot synchronisation into the preset writer.
components.confidence: Round trip tested on two reference files; one generated preset loaded on the pedal.

components.name: Preparing the song: guitar isolation and a clean reference guitar
components.purpose: Extract the guitar from the recording and supply a clean guitar recording to compare against.
components.works: Separation runs in seconds, sections are found and a library of clean guitar clips is indexed. A stress curve on a synthetic mix is recorded. Since 21 October: a clean guitar can be rebuilt from a separated song and a calibration profile of one guitar exists. The ablation shows the winning drive model mostly stays the same under other clean-guitar inputs.
components.missing: Any quality score on real songs and any measurement of the clean-guitar choice's benefit (the rebuild has never been compared with a library clean guitar on the same search). The rebuild is approximate and the level convention is undecided.
components.problem: The rebuilt clean guitar's contribution is unmeasured by ear (seven blind packs unrated); separation quality on real songs is unknown, and the human has ruled out separator work.
components.confidence: Synthetic mix only; one real song without a quality score.

components.name: Judging tone similarity: comparison measures and block measuring
components.purpose: Say how close two guitar sounds are, and describe how each block behaves.
components.works: Five comparison measures run. The lead admitted one (the multi-resolution spectral measure, version 2) for single blocks with a known clean recording (0.990 on a held-out split); the human has not approved it, judged the model built on it unusable, and on hard same-performance pairs it is at chance. The learned listening measure orders effect models on the same performance in agreement with the ear and is the de facto ranker. A block-presence detector exists (cabinet and gain stage pass; the rest miss). A cabinet-response estimator is promising. Block fingerprints exist for 602 models.
components.missing: A measure for the no-recording song case; reliable detection of delay, reverb and modulation blocks.
components.problem: No measure is approved by the human; the learned measure ranks the final candidates as an interim default and has no ear validation against a separated guitar (its blind session was answered with a verdict, not ranks).
components.next: Decide whether to score the stem-validation pack; the chain predictor may replace measure-led ranking if it works.
components.confidence: Real Helix renders from Native; held-out splits scored once; ear agreement only for ordering models on the same performance; not real songs.

components.name: Searching for the preset, the colour stage and the song-to-preset pipeline
components.purpose: Try candidate presets, score them against the target and return the best preset.
components.works: A hybrid method with family specialists (cabinet and equaliser, time-based, modulation, amp, gain) runs on Native. On 96 sealed items it named the category 88.5 percent and the model 77.1 percent of the time with settings error 0.101 (attempt 3). A chain builder exists, tested with fake engines only. A full drive search plus knob fine-tune is run on seven songs from a rebuilt clean guitar (heard once, openly). A measured-pedal mode is built and simulated only. Since 25 October: a bounded equaliser fit, a reverb candidate grid and comparison pages, and a blind reverb estimator (decay and mix from a stem's note tails) exist as pilots.
components.missing: No reverb model and no colour stage in any matcher; the estimator reads a real tail on 2 of 7 stems. Only the drive slot is matched; the first blind listening of those matches was negative. Chain builder on a real engine, snapshots, a one-command tool.
components.problem: The first blind listening of drive-only matches on real songs was negative, and the reverb has no model.
components.next: Read the chain predictor, then decide the reverb model with the human.
components.confidence: Synthetic known-answer data (96 sealed items, Gate 2 now closed as superseded) on Native; seven songs heard once openly and five songs once blind (negative); reverb estimator on 189 known reverbs; the pedal never probed.

components.name: Testing, benchmarks and listening
components.purpose: Provide the measurements and listening tests that decide whether the product works.
components.works: The evidence ledger, smoke tests, engine agreement measurements, the 96-item known-answer set with its runner and frozen pass rule, three full attempt results (the third meets all checks on paper; the human judged the model unusable), a blind A/B session tool and seven rated short sessions. Since 25 October: a sealed 120-item Gate 3 set with a verifier and a scorer that refuses to run without a launch reference, a blind ranking-pack builder and scorer, and pre-registered pilots (reverb) scored by the script.
components.missing: Approved Gate 3 bars and any scoring of the sealed set, a blind rating of the song matches that is scored, and sessions long enough to beat the listener's own repeat noise on pair trials (7 of 12).
components.problem: Gate 3 bars are proposed, not approved, so the sealed set cannot be scored.
components.next: Human rules on the bars; benchmark scores once.
components.confidence: Hardware measurements of engine agreement; full known-answer runs on Native (Gate 2, closed as superseded); sealed set built but unscored; listening short and directional.

components.name: Learning from data
components.purpose: Learn from rendered pairs to name a block and its settings, so the search needs fewer renders.
components.works: A drive predictor narrows the search (85 percent right first on 48 blind targets, evidence class D) and six more slots have trained predictors from about 240,000 single-block renders. An overnight job is rendering about 40,000 drive, equaliser and reverb chains to train a predictor of the product chain (37,998 done at 2026-10-26 16:23).
components.missing: The chain predictor has no result; the slot predictors for other slots are out of scope and failed inside chains; nothing is verified on the sealed set.
components.problem: The open bet has no result yet, and single-block predictors do not transfer to chains.
components.next: Let training finish, then read the seven-song table and propose how to score it.
components.confidence: Measurement on Helix Native renders; the new job has produced no result; no ear test of any predictor-driven match.

components.name: Foundations: installation, licensing and the working process
components.purpose: Make the project installable, legally clean and organised.
components.works: Installs on this Mac, licence checks pass, and the board, evidence ledger and gates are in use. A file now pins song-match defaults to what the human approved.
components.missing: Windows and Linux checks, recorded licence-agreement findings, and tidier board lines (T223, T228 and T230 lines are behind the record).
components.problem: Licence-agreement findings are unrecorded; some board lines are stale.
components.next: Update the board; owner records the licence findings.
components.confidence: Tests and a licence scan; one operating system.

glossary.definition: Direct Input: a clean, unprocessed guitar recording, before any amp or effects.
Digital Signal Processing: the audio calculations inside amps and effects.
The software licence agreement shown when installing a product.
An optimisation algorithm used to search for suitable settings.
The Line 6 guitar-effects pedal this project targets.
Line 6's software version of the Helix sounds; it runs as a plugin and renders audio offline.
Line 6's editing program for the pedal; it also imports preset files.
A saved sound: a chain of amp, cabinet and effect blocks with their settings (an .hlx file).
One of up to three stored variations of a preset that the pedal can switch between.
The software running inside the pedal.
The score the optimiser tries to lower: how different two sounds are. Lower is a closer match.
The loss: the combined measures of how similar two guitar sounds are.
Test audio made by ordinary software effects instead of Helix. Useful for early checks; not proof the method works on Helix.
A test set made by rendering presets we already know through Helix, so we can check whether the tool recovers them.
Test items not used when tuning, so the result is not flattered by tuning.
A test of whether a measure puts the true preset first among many candidates.
What is left when one recording is subtracted from another that should match. Reported in decibels below the signal; the more negative, the closer.
Decibel, a logarithmic loudness or level-difference scale.
A cabinet setting that adds the first short echoes of the room.
Splitting a full mix into instruments so the guitar can be analysed alone.
One element in a preset's chain: an amp, cabinet, drive pedal, delay and so on.
The project's append-only record of measured runs; a claim without a row did not happen.
A milestone with a written checklist and a human sign-off.
A listening test where the listener does not know which option is which.
Reading the pedal's settings back after writing them to confirm they match.
A control message that moves one knob or switch from software.
Short for firmware, the pedal's built-in software. The pedal was on version 3.50 until 2026-10-15 and is now on 3.80.
Play a test signal through a preset and record the audio that comes out.
The one-off step that teaches Helix Native a new chain: the preset file is loaded into its editor and the resulting state is recorded.
Agreement between the two engines: the same preset is rendered on both and the recordings are compared.
Several copies of Helix Native running at once, each rendering a different candidate, to finish a batch sooner.
Extra audio played before the part that is recorded, so delays and reverbs start from the same state every time.
The two signal paths of the HX Stomp. Using both at once renders two chains in one pass.
Two amp settings that add a mains-hum style noise. The noise runs freely, so it differs between renders of the same preset.
The last message a control program sends to the pedal when it is done. Without it the pedal stays in editing mode and its blocks cannot be edited by hand.
One candidate setting tried by the search: it is rendered and then scored against the target.
A reference preset file the owner exported from HX Edit or Native, used to check that our own files follow the same layout.
Real elapsed time on a clock, as opposed to computing time.
How often the true preset is ranked first among the candidates (the look-alikes). Higher is better; guessing among 20 gives 0.05.
A stored set of single-block Native setups, one per pedal effect model, used to build and render candidate presets quickly.
The Mac's audio system. When it fails, no sound can be sent to or recorded from the pedal.
A candidate preset that differs slightly from the true one (a nearby setting or a neighbouring model); used to test whether a measure can tell near matches apart.
An effect that changes its sound on its own over time (for example a free-running chorus), so two renders never cancel exactly.

A baseline search that tries 300 random settings and keeps the best, judged by the same trusted score. It scores high here because the tool has only 300 tries over a pool of 47 effect models and the score is a good judge, so even random guessing often lands on the right model. Earlier notes called it random search.
A baseline that sets every knob to the middle of its range and picks nothing cleverly. It shows what a do-nothing guess scores.
A separate method for one family of effects (gain, linear, dynamics, time-based, modulation) with its own measurements and search, instead of one general method for everything.
A group of effects that behave alike: gain (drive, fuzz, amp), linear (cabinet, equaliser), dynamics (compressor, gate), time-based (delay, reverb), modulation (chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo).
A range for a measured difference, built by re-sampling the 96 items many times. If the whole range sits on the good side of a line, the difference is reliable at the stated confidence.
A check run inside a long job that renders a fixed test now and then and stops the job if the result has drifted, so a corrupted render cannot be scored as real.
The planned stage that decides which kinds of block a tone needs, orders them by common patterns learned from real presets, and then fills each slot using the single-block methods.
A fresh known-answer set, made with the same generator and the same frozen rules but a new random seed, because the first set has now been seen.
A short recording of a speaker cabinet and microphone that can reproduce that cabinet's sound by convolution. A cabinet block in the pedal uses one.
Helix Native starts each session in one of two slightly different rounding modes. The difference is tiny (rounding level) but can break exact cancellation tests.
A one-sample shift or short burst in the audio coming back from the pedal over its USB connection, which makes a render differ slightly from an identical earlier one.
A free, Apache-2.0 licensed program from Spotify that writes down the notes in a recording. Used here to turn a separated guitar part into notes, which are then played back as a clean guitar.

A stand-in clean guitar made for a song that has none: the notes found in the separated guitar are replayed using real clean guitar notes (from a library or from the player's own calibration session).
A one-off calibration of one guitar: its normal playing level, its tone compared with the library guitars, and a bank of its own notes.
Decibels relative to full scale: how loud a digital signal is. 0 is the loudest possible; -36 is much quieter than -28.
A learned listening measure (a neural network embedding) used here to order candidate presets by how close they sound to the target. Lower distance is closer.
A trained program that looks at a sound and guesses which block model and settings made it. Used to narrow the search.
A fixed position in the signal chain: drive, amp, cabinet, modulation, delay, reverb, equaliser, in that order. Each slot is optional.
How often the correct answer is the first choice, or among the first three choices.
After the block model is chosen, a local search that adjusts only its knobs to bring the render closer to the target.
A loudness measure that follows how loud something sounds. Listening comparisons are level-matched with it so louder does not win.
How well a trained predictor works on a guitarist whose playing it never saw in training. The honest test for a tool that will be used by someone else.

How strong a claim's evidence is, from the audit: A blind with a sealed set and a bar registered first; B blind on an unsealed set; C an open listen by the human (knowing which is which); D numbers only, on an unadmitted measure or without a bar; E no evidence.
How often the listener gives the same answer when a blind pair is repeated. The human's is 7 of 12 across the sessions so far, so small sessions cannot resolve small differences.
A listening session where the listener knows which candidate is which. It can flatter a method; a blind session cannot.
A test set generated after the bars are registered, with hashes recorded, that no agent reads before the one scoring run.

Two runs whose clean-guitar input differs (other notes, tone or level). A distance between their renders and the target mixes the effect of the guitar with the effect of the preset, so it cannot say which preset is closer.
The early combination of three tone measures used before any measure was admitted. Never admitted; at chance on hard pairs; still the default re-score of the block matcher.
The third library guitarist's clean recordings, held back from every training set and every search so a sealed test can use them.
How much a listening measure moves with a change of clean guitar compared with a knob move. Above 1 means the guitar matters more than the knob; the learned measure scored 30 for small knob moves.
Equaliser: a tone control that boosts or cuts parts of the frequency spectrum, such as bass or treble.
An effect that adds the sound of a space (room, plate, hall) after the guitar. Decay is how long the tail lasts; Mix is how much of it is blended in.
The chain the product builds, as redefined by the human on 2026-10-25: a drive effect, then an equaliser, then a reverb. No amp, cabinet or delay for now.
The analysis and the reading of its result were written down, with a hash, before any answer was seen, so the result cannot be bent to fit.
A calculation that reads a reverb's decay and amount from the tails left at the end of notes in a recording, without knowing the reverb setting.
Sound from the band (bass, drums, vocals) that the guitar separator fails to remove. It can look like a reverb tail and hide a real one.
A list in the repository of method settings the human has ruled on, with the human's words; a test fails if the code's defaults drift from it.
Evidence classes from the audit: C is an open listen (the listener knew which was which); B is blind on an unsealed set. See 'evidence class'.
