engines._about: Wording for the 'Engines: what each can do and how fast' section. The capability verdicts are curated judgements from the ledger, DECISIONS, notes and board (cite them inline; they become links). Numbers written as {t:key:engine} are filled from the ledger every run, so they cannot go stale. 'fw350': true appends 'verified on fw 3.50, recheck on 3.80 pending' until a ledger row shows the claim re-checked on firmware 3.80; then the flag is cleared (done for parameter changes and two-path rendering on 2026-10-16). All timings and the 100-test estimates are computed by scripts/engine_timing.py; nothing about time is written by hand here.
engines.units: Times are in seconds (s), minutes (min) and hours (h). A render is one pass of a test signal through a preset, recorded as audio. A score is one comparison of a rendered candidate against the target tone (lower is better). A capture is the one-off step that teaches Helix Native a new chain, by loading the preset file into its editor and recording its state. A parity check renders one preset on both engines and compares the two recordings. Estimates are 100 times the newest measured time; every estimate says which measurement it uses and its date. Native pool figures use 6 hosts (the owner approved that cap on 2026-10-16) and count a render plus its score as one test; pedal figures from firmware 3.80 are marked as such.

render_2s.label: One render of a 2 s test clip
render_2s.means: Play a 2 second test signal through a preset and record the result.

search_test.label: One search test, 2 s clip
search_test.means: One candidate in a search. Native: a render plus its score through the 6-host pool. Pedal: one search trial with the T061 speed options (3 s clip), render side only.

search_test_10s.label: One search test, 10 s clip
search_test_10s.means: The same with a 10 s excerpt. Pedal: the trial before the T061 speed options, for comparison.

session.label: Pedal session overhead
session.means: Opening the pedal engine, restoring the original preset and checking it byte for byte. Once per batch since T061.

verify.label: Verify one finalist on the pedal
verify.means: Write a finalist whole to the pedal and render it twice with 10 s clips.

render_10s.label: One render of a 10 s clip
render_10s.means: The same, with a 10 second excerpt (the size a song-section search uses).

score.label: One comparison (score) of a candidate against a target
score.means: Measure how far a rendered candidate is from the target tone. From the trust check's scoring-cost rows: the three signal-processing terms added, render excluded.

parity.label: One parity comparison (per preset)
parity.means: Render one preset on both engines, then analyse how closely the two recordings agree.

smoke.label: One engine smoke test
smoke.means: The quick end-to-end check that an engine loads a preset and returns sound.

search_run.label: A search run, per trial
search_run.means: Native: the run's wall clock divided by its renders, engine start-up included. Pedal: seconds per trial of the default search run (3 s clip).

load.label: One preset load or model change
load.means: Stomp: one whole-document write of a generated preset. Native: load a stored template.

capture.label: First-time capture of a new chain
capture.means: Native only: teach the engine a chain it has not seen. Once per chain.

probe_pass.label: One probe pass through an engine
probe_pass.means: Play the block-probe test signals through one block and record them.

probe_analysis.label: One probe analysis (offline)
probe_analysis.means: Check the probe analysis code against known software blocks; no engine involved.

trial.label: One search trial (render + score)
trial.means: One candidate setting: render it, then score it. Scoring time is taken from the score row above.

combined_testing.label: Combined: testing
combined_testing.means: Engine smoke test per engine, and one parity comparison per preset on both.

combined_comparison.label: Combined: comparison
combined_comparison.means: Scoring a candidate against a target.

combined_modelling.label: Combined: modelling
combined_modelling.means: One search trial plus a capture (Native) or a preset write (Stomp).

capabilities.capability: Load a generated preset file (.hlx) directly

stomp.verdict: Yes. The file is compiled and written whole into the pedal's working memory, then read back parameter by parameter before anything is rendered; about 40 whole writes, all read back as written (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp T056 outcomes). 4 of 4 generated files were written and rendered (ledger 2026-10-14T23:47:43+00:00). Re-checked on firmware 3.80: 9 of 9 whole writes landed and the pedal was restored byte for byte (ledger 2026-10-15T23:40:20+00:00). Takes {t:load:stomp}.

native.verdict: Yes, with no person, on macOS: a script drops the file into Native's editor and records the state as a template, then renders from the template (ledger 2026-10-14T23:58:32+00:00). A stored template loads in {t:load:native}; a chain never seen before needs a capture first (see below).

capabilities.capability: Export or save a preset file

stomp.verdict: Our own writer produces the .hlx; a human imports it in HX Edit (accepted, ledger 2026-10-14T17:38:00+00:00). The engine never saves to the pedal's flash memory, by policy: it edits the working copy only and puts the original preset back (DECISIONS 2026-10-14 stomp-engine, T003 hardware batch and T004).

native.verdict: Not done and not needed for matching: the generated .hlx is the source, and Native's captured state is kept as a local template, not exported as a file.

stomp.verdict: Yes, at full resolution. Parameters are set in place and checked by read-back to within one hundred-thousandth of the parameter's range (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 stomp-engine, T051 whole-write readback). Re-checked on firmware 3.80: 20 in-place loads of six random amp parameters each ended with a clean full read-back (ledger 2026-10-15T23:57:03+00:00).

native.verdict: Only parameters given a MIDI control number at capture, in 128 steps across each range; everything else stays as captured. Inside that grid it equals a freshly captured file almost exactly (ledger 2026-10-15T20:46:58+00:00). On the 8-block test chain 54 of 63 mapped parameters moved the sound (ledger 2026-10-15T21:31:30+00:00).

capabilities.capability: Change models (swap an amp, cab or effect)

stomp.verdict: Yes. Any model or layout change is one whole write with read-back, never the pedal's own model command (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp T056 outcomes). {t:load:stomp} per write. On firmware 3.80, one block from each of the six effect categories and two amps with impulse-response cabinets were built and read back (ledger 2026-10-15T23:40:20+00:00).

native.verdict: Yes, from the block library: a model is loaded by its id from a stored template, with no new capture. Chains of several blocks still need a capture ({t:capture:native}, once per chain). Mono only (ledger 2026-10-16T15:25:12+00:00).

capabilities.capability: Switch blocks on and off by script

stomp.verdict: Yes. Bypass is toggled in place with a MIDI control (the delay's bypass moved with CC 110, ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00), and is part of every whole write.

native.verdict: Yes. Each block's bypass is a MIDI control number in the captured template; one capture reproduces every bypass pattern almost exactly (-328.7 dB against files captured one by one, ledger 2026-10-15T21:31:30+00:00). Only chains captured since 2026-10-15 have it; older templates keep fixed bypass states (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, Native phase 2 block bypass).

stomp.verdict: Path A and Path B give twice the renders per pass (measured on firmware 3.50, ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00; not re-measured on 3.80). The earlier gap of -18 to -22 dB between two-path and single-path renders was a layout bug, fixed by writing the layout the way the pedal's own editor stores it: on firmware 3.80 our two-path load now nulls against the editor-saved preset at -85.7 dB, equal to that preset's own repeat floor, against -9.3 dB before (ledger 2026-10-16T01:06:38+00:00). A two-path pass also matches each chain rendered alone: Path A -72.9 dB (repeat floor -68.7), Path B -52.6 dB (floor -42.7). The rule that two-path renders are compared only with two-path renders was lifted on 2026-10-16 (DECISIONS 2026-10-16 stomp-engine, T063 two-path layout). Not tested: crossover and A/B split types; a pass with its own Path B input is refused by the compiler. Two-chain passes equal single-chain passes on firmware 3.80 for the tested chains (ledger 2026-10-16T15:44:03+00:00). The code that renders two variants per pass was then compared on the pedal's audio against serial renders: path A/B nulls of -78.5/-60.4 and -85.1/-78.6 dB, each below the serial repeat floor, about 1.7 s per variant (ledger 2026-10-16T20:28:58+00:00).

native.verdict: Out of scope: two-path passes on Native will not be built (owner's decision, 2026-10-16); Native renders in parallel on 6 hosts instead. Block-serial chaining equals one instance at -67 to -79 dB above 20 Hz on the tested chains (ledger 2026-10-15T19:21:10+00:00).

capabilities.capability: Use the whole block and model catalog

stomp.verdict: In principle any compatible model can be written with no capture, because the pedal runs it itself. Tried so far: the amps, cabs, drives and delays in the test presets on firmware 3.50, and one block from each effect category and two amps with impulse-response cabinets on firmware 3.80 (ledger 2026-10-15T23:40:20+00:00). Whether the 90 models gated by firmware now work on 3.80 has not been rechecked (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp firmware upgrade, human).

native.verdict: Through the per-block library, now captured: 605 of the pedal's 607 models (the other 2, a transient shaper and a poly bass whammy, are refused by Native 3.82), each replayed in a fresh host (ledger 2026-10-16T15:25:12+00:00). Time-like and rate settings were re-captured with narrower control ranges (ledger 2026-10-16T16:04:28+00:00, 2026-10-16T17:54:03+00:00). Not captured by design: routing models and the second cabinet of a dual-cab block.

stomp.verdict: {t:render_2s:stomp} for a 2 s clip (the pedal plays the audio in real time); a 10 s clip is {t:render_10s:stomp}. Two-chain passes double throughput (see above). Measured on firmware 3.80: a 3 s clip takes 3.67 s (ledger 2026-10-15T23:48:50+00:00). A search trial with the T061 speed options takes {t:search_test:stomp} (render side only). See the speed-up row below for the search and verification gains.

native.verdict: {t:render_2s:native} for a 2 s clip and {t:render_10s:native} for a 10 s clip including 3 s of pre-roll. A pool of 6 parallel hosts (the approved cap) finishes a search test of a 2 s clip, render and score together, in {t:search_test:native}, and one of a 10 s clip in {t:search_test_10s:native} (timing tables below).

stomp.verdict: Snapshot values are written into the document and must equal the block values (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 snapshot values, lead on stomp-engine T051). Switching snapshots by MIDI (CC 69) recalls the stored values (ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00). Switching during a render is not tested.

native.verdict: Native renders the block values and ignores snapshot values when a file is loaded (ledger 2026-10-15T19:42:45+00:00). Snapshots are not switched in Native.

both.verdict: Measured on firmware 3.80 (ledger 2026-10-16T02:31:10+00:00, 2026-10-16T15:36:36+00:00, 2026-10-16T16:18:35+00:00): amps cancel at -37.5 to -47.5 dB and cabinets at -35.4 to -37.4 dB (pass line -30 dB); dynamics and equalisers pass. For delays, reverbs and modulation the comparison is by echo timing, decay and modulation rate rather than cancellation. Accepted result: Native stands in for amps, cabinets, dynamics, equalisers, drives except Bitcrusher-type, delays, four reverb types, Hall above 500 Hz, and the modulation effects; the pedal still checks Ganymede-type reverbs, Hall on bass-heavy material, Bitcrusher-type drives and cabinet Early Reflections. A suggested delay-time scaling of under 1 in 100 was rejected (it was Native's control step).

stomp.verdict: The session-release lock is fixed (T059). Before the fix any control session left the pedal's block editing locked until USB was unplugged, even after the firmware 3.80 upgrade (ledger 2026-10-15T22:36:17+00:00). The helper now sends HX Edit's session close, and a person confirmed the blocks were editable afterwards (ledger 2026-10-15T23:03:12+00:00); the close was answered on every channel in a later smoke run (ledger 2026-10-15T23:20:15+00:00). One earlier control wedge that needed a power cycle is still unexplained (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 HX Stomp priorities, human). Pedal verification on 2026-10-17 (ledger 2026-10-17T17:37:28+00:00): setting truth 20 of 40, repeatability 12 of 17; the audio stream is unstable for about 0.7 s after start, amps carry state between renders, four models are refused, and a one-sample slip remains in about 1 render in 90. Pre-roll is now 1.0 s (2.0 s with an amp). No pedal result counts until that slip is handled.

native.verdict: Memory growth and crashes are fixed: the host stays at about 3.0 GB and repeats are identical to -313 dB (ledger 2026-10-15T18:54:10+00:00; DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, host memory). About 1 host process in 10 rendered every chain differently until a start-up check (the host canary) began replacing such hosts (ledger 2026-10-16T00:25:27+00:00); Native results from before 2026-10-16 are kept as history. Captures need a logged-in screen session. Verification on 2026-10-17 (ledger 2026-10-17T17:35:18+00:00): repeat renders 216 of 216 at worst -161.5 dB after three engine fixes (baked controls no longer sent, hosts in the other numeric mode re-prepared, an amp state latch at open); setting truth 116 of 120 pairs (ledger 2026-10-17T17:38:13+00:00); a sentinel in the engine catches a forced drift (ledger 2026-10-17T17:29:36+00:00). Native results from before these fixes used the earlier engine.

stomp.verdict: Measured on firmware 3.80 (T061, docs/notes/stomp-speed.md): a search trial went from 10.861 s to 3.765 s (ledger 2026-10-16T00:17:11+00:00, 10 trials, 3 s clips, readback every 10 loads, measured tail waits). Per-test session overhead fell from 3.812 s to 0.772 s (ledger 2026-10-15T23:47:32+00:00). A verification finalist (whole write plus two 10 s renders) improved only from 29.23 s to 24.65 s (ledger 2026-10-16T00:10:35+00:00). The shorter tail waits are only equal to the long waits with Hum and Ripple at 0 (ledger 2026-10-15T23:55:24+00:00). The search now uses these options by default (task T062), but it has not been timed on the pedal.

native.verdict: Capture fell from about 31 s to 1.2 s per chain in one session, and 216 chains took 84.6 s (ledger 2026-10-15T23:57:11+00:00). A pool of 6 hosts ran 9.9 tests per second on 2 s clips and 4.6 on 10 s clips (ledger 2026-10-16T00:38:03+00:00); 10 hosts ran 13.1 and 6.4 but with memory pressure and swapping, so the owner capped the pool at 6 on 2026-10-16.
